acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::revolve` returns `KernelError::InvalidInput` (never a panic, never a backend error, and no revolve is attempted) when the axis is not in the profile's plane: its direction is not perpendicular to the plane normal, or its origin is farther than the tolerance from the plane. Tests: the rectangle x 10..20, z 0..5 with (1) the z axis moved to origin (0, 1, 0), (2) direction (0, 1, 1), (3) direction (0, 1, 0). The error message names the axis and the plane.

`Kernel::revolve` returns `InvalidInput` when the profile has points strictly on both sides of the axis, beyond the tolerance. Test: the rectangle x −5..5, z 0..5 about the z axis. The error message says that the profile crosses the axis.

A profile that touches the axis is still valid. Test: the rectangle x 0..10, z 0..5, full turn about the z axis, gives volume 500π ≈ 1570.7963 (relative 1e-6), bounding box (−10, −10, 0)–(10, 10, 5) (within 1e-6), and 3 faces.
Inputs within the tolerance are accepted. Test: the z axis with origin (0, 1e-9, 0) revolves the rectangle x 10..20, z 0..5 a full turn to volume 1500π (relative 1e-6).
`revolve_feature` passes these errors through. Test: `Cut` against `make_box((−25, −25, 0), (50, 50, 10))`, with the axis direction (0, 1, 1), returns `InvalidInput`.
`Kernel::revolve`'s doc comment lists the new error cases. All existing revolve tests pass unchanged.

No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies. Every new or changed shim function is `noexcept` and catches C++ exceptions. Every new `unsafe` block is in `ffi` and documented.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
